newsitem.title: UK: Caffeine may slow blood flow to brain-researcher.
newsitem.headline: Caffeine may slow blood flow to brain-researcher.

text.p: A possibility that caffeine could slow blood flow to the brain has prompted a study by Britain's defence ministry which is concerned about the speed of combat pilots' reactions, a researcher said on Wednesday.
Just two cups of coffee could in some circumstances reduce the blood flow by 15 to 20 percent, according to David Kerr, a consultant physician at the Royal Bournemouth Hospital in southern England.
"The MOD (Ministry of Defence) is interested to find out if caffeine affects the intellectual performance of, for example, pilots," he said.
The study, undertaken jointly by the ministry and the hospital, began last month and is expected to be completed in four to six months.
A team of healthy volunteers is being used to measure the effects of caffeine on brain power at the government's Defence Evaluation and Research Agency.

The agency said the study had just begun and no conclusion had been reached yet. A spokesman for Britain's Royal Air Force said: "We do not believe we have a problem with pilots drinking coffee at this time."
But military chiefs want to know if caffeine could be linked with role behind the loss of 40 aircraft since 1993 during training missions.
